construction: 524 parts in 9 steps across 9 sections: `Bottom section` and `Center support` (Technic bricks and plates as the spine), `Nose gear` with its `Switch arm`, `Nose section` (the SNOT nose with the instrument slope), `Left wing` and `Right wing` (mirrored plate deltas), `Tail fin`, plus the 89762 canopy, 54200 cheese slopes along the fuselage edges and the two 43121 engines in the root.
interfaces: 429 studs up, 84 sideways (nose wedges and fuselage sides), 7 angled. The wings pin to the spine through their 1×2 Technic bricks; the nose stacks on the front plates; the fin's base plate sits on the spine; the canopy sits on the cockpit rim.
lesson: A Creator jet: a Technic-brick spine with pins carries a studs-up System skin, delta plate wings with Technic-brick roots, a SNOT nose with a cone spike, a one-stud slope fin, twin 43121 engines side by side at the tail and a retracting nose gear. Measured: span 41 studs, length 50, height 17, 524 parts, 16% Technic.
parent_context: `5892 - main.ldr` places it at the origin with the identity matrix; the nose points −X, so LeoCAD's front view shows the side.
reuse_notes: Use it as the template for a mid-size jet: length 1.2× span, delta wings two plates thick, engines at the rear, fin one stud thick. Build the Technic spine first, then hang wings, nose and fin on it before closing the skin.
